commit.message:
fix(mermaid-to-proverif): read ProVerif results correctly and test forward secrecy properly (#367)

Checked with ProVerif 2.05 on the shipped example:

- Reachability guidance was inverted in five places. ProVerif checks
  `not event(e)`, so it prints `is false` when the event IS reachable (the
  shipped example prints exactly that); `is true` is the broken-model case.
- The example's Q3 (injective authentication, R's view) reports false: the
  drawn protocol has no responder challenge, so a replayed msg1 completes
  another R-run; the weak correspondence holds. The model matches the
  diagram, so document this as a genuine finding rather than call the model
  one where every query holds.
- The forward-secrecy pattern leaked the long-term keys at the start, which
  lets the attacker impersonate and makes secrecy false for any
  authenticated protocol. Leak them after the sessions, in phase 1, where
  the example's secrecy queries hold.
- Remove two dangling pointers: SKILL.md promised unlinkability guidance no
  reference has, and cited the example as a forward-secrecy worked example
  although it only has a comment.

A test keeps the guidance consistent with ProVerif's output.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: kz-tob <kara.zaffarano@trailofbits.com>
